answer: A harvest prices admission better than a certificate does. A newcomer plants a vine and earns nothing until it has lived through real seasons; the stake is read by growth rings the way a sawyer dates a timber, and a timber cured overnight fails the ring count. Weight is then paid in saffron, picked by hand at dawn, one flower per unit of real work, so a thousand keys require a thousand mornings and no machine hurries that harvest. Auditors count every planting once: one vine, one timber, one measure of saffron, and repeat filings from the same ground add nothing.
